title: The normalization algebra of local curve branches
statement:
For a reduced one-dimensional Noetherian local commutative ring $R$,
let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$ be all its distinct minimal
prime ideals. Here reduced means that $x^n=0$ with $n\ge1$ implies
$x=0$, local means that there is a unique maximal ideal, Noetherian
is as in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and dimension is Krull
dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A prime ideal is a proper ideal $\mathfrak p$ such that
$xy\in\mathfrak p$ implies $x\in\mathfrak p$ or $y\in\mathfrak p$.
A minimal prime is a prime ideal minimal under inclusion among all
prime ideals;
there are finitely many by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal]
with the zero ideal.

Put $A_a=R/\mathfrak p_a$ and $K_a=\operatorname{Frac}(A_a)$,
the localization of the domain $A_a$ at its nonzero elements
[def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Define

$$
Q(R)=\prod_{a=1}^t K_a,
\qquad
B(R)=\prod_{a=1}^t\overline{A_a}^{\,K_a}.
$$

The factor $\overline{A_a}^{\,K_a}$ is the subring of $K_a$
of elements integral over $A_a$, with integral closure as in
[def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. These are the integral closures
used in [def-sc-normalization], [def-fin-normalization-extension].
Both products have coordinatewise ring operations.
The map $R\to B(R)$ sends $r$ to the tuple whose $a$-th coordinate
is the image of $r+\mathfrak p_a$ in $\overline{A_a}^{\,K_a}$;
it is the product of the quotient maps followed by the canonical
maps into these integral closures. This equips $B(R)$ with its
$R$-algebra structure and defines the branch algebra without
assuming its finiteness or a decomposition into local rings.
